# Access matrix: who may call each route registered on the server's mux.
#
# One line per route, and every column spelled out: there are no defaults.
# TestAccessTableCoversEveryRoute (access_test.go) holds these lines and the registered
# routes to each other one to one; TestAccessMatrix sends every route as every kind of
# caller and checks the answer against its line. A new route fails both until it has a
# line here: add one and decide each column.
#
# METHOD PATH  the pattern as registered; ANY for a pattern without a method.
# scope=       public: open without signing in; the other columns are then yes and
#              plan=none, since nothing about the caller is checked.
#              read, operate, admin: the level the route is mounted with (rd, op, adm),
#              held against the user's role and, for an API token, its scope as well.
#              token: API tokens only, a browser session gets 401 (the MCP endpoint;
#              its tools check their own level in internal/mcpserver).
# tokens=      yes: an API token passes within its scope. no: the handler refuses every
#              token (sessionOnly and the like). admin: a token needs admin scope here
#              although a session needs less. body: refused for a token when the body
#              carries a way in (sshAuthorizedKeys in PATCH /settings). own: a token may
#              only act on what the instance made itself, not on an upload or an archive
#              fetched from offsite (instance backup restore); the test sends it an
#              uploaded one.
# support=     the hoster's support session (an admin): yes, no (supportRefused in
#              support.go), or body: refused when the body carries what it may not set
#              (the instance's SSH keys or the log history in PATCH /settings, a custom
#              image in a manifest). Refused by what a backup holds rather than the body,
#              and so not tried here: restore-new of a backup with a custom image
#              (TestSupportRestoresNoCustomImage).
# confined=    a principal limited to particular projects (a token with a project list,
#              a user whose global role is none). project: its level in the path's
#              project decides. any: its level in any of its projects opens the route
#              (routesForAnyProject). yes: open to confined tokens and users
#              (instanceRoutesForConfined). users: open to confined users' sessions only
#              (instanceRoutesForConfinedUsers). no: refused.
# suspended=   yes: still answered while the hoster suspends the instance
#              (routesWhileSuspended); no: refused then.
# plan=        offsite: refused unless the plan has offsite targets, except for the
#              hoster's own target; none: the plan doesn't gate the route.
# twofactor=   yes: still answered to a session that has to set up a second factor
#              first (routesWhileTwoFactorSetup); no: refused to it.

GET    /api/v1/health                                                scope=public  tokens=yes   support=yes  confined=yes     suspended=yes plan=none twofactor=yes
